subject: Solaris: swingline 2-year prepay structure + SLA credit exception
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@solaris.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ian Cross <ian.cross@solaristrade.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: 2-yr prepay discussion — need for swingline + SLA relief

Jordan —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Solaris ran the numbers and we can commit to a 24-month prepay but only if we can structure a swingline (front-loaded Year 1) to cover an aggressive GTM ramp and if redwood can offer an SLA credit buffer for the first 6 months while we validate traffic patterns.

Key asks:
- 2-year prepay, total committed spend $1.2M
- Year 1: ~65% of total (to cover initial spikes), Year 2: ~35%
- Discount target: 15% off list (we see similar vendors at ~14%)
- SLA credit: one-time 30% credit on monthly overage for first 6 months if latency/SLOs missed
- Need an SOW and draft contract to circulate to legal next week

Attaching our projected usage file so you can see the ramp buckets.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) accept swingline front-loading, 2) provide an SLA credit exception, and 3) provide a draft SOW this week?

Thanks —
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Partnerships
SolarisAI

Attachments: Solaris_usage_by_product_v1.csv
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@solaris.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: 2-yr prepay discussion — need for swingline + SLA relief

Maya —

Appreciate the clarity and the file. Good news: we can structure a swingline (front-load Year 1) and we have flexibility on contract language to support a short-term SLA credit mechanism. A few things to flag from our side so legal/commercial can try to move quickly:

- Pricing: list-level discount requests at 15% are above our self-serve bands for deals this size. I can push for an exception but need buy-in from RevOps/Finance on the true-up cadence and risk controls.
- True-up: finance will want a 90-day usage true-up (standard) to reconcile the front-loaded payment vs. actual consumption.
- SLA credit: we can scope a one-time credit policy for the first 6 months, but we typically cap credits at a percentage of monthly invoice. I will surface a proposed cap and the internal approval path.
- Deliverables: I attached a Draft_SOW_Solaris_2yr.pdf stub and a usage gap workbook (Solaris_Usage_Gap_v3.xlsx) with recommended bucketing for our pricing model.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal approval thread (cc'd) to confirm discount cap and true-up cadence.
2) If approved, I will send a redlined SOW + Term Sheet for Solaris legal by EOD Monday.

Lauren / Karthik — tagging you both. Solaris is requesting 15% off list + 30% one-time SLA credit for first 6 months; they also want a 65/35 year split (Year1/Year2). Can we approve a path to 13% with a 90-day true-up and SLA credit capped at 30% monthly credit but limited to one month-equivalent max across the first 6 months? If not, what is the max discount & SLA cap we can offer as a one-time exception?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_SOW_Solaris_2yr.pdf; Solaris_Usage_Gap_v3.xlsx
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: 2-yr prepay discussion — need for swingline + SLA relief

Jordan —

Thanks for the laydown. High level thoughts:

- Discount: our standard discount curve on a two-year commit at $1.2M total would typically be 8–10%. For a swingline structure that concentrates spend in Year 1 we can stretch to 12% as an approved commercial concession, provided Finance signs off on the reconciliation mechanism.
- SLA credit: we can agree to a one-time credit mechanism for the first 6 months, but we need to tie it to concrete SLOs (p90 latency, availability) and cap total exposure. I am comfortable with a monthly cap equal to 30% of that month's bill, but not with an aggregate cap that exceeds 1x monthly invoice across the 6-month window.
- True-up cadence: 90 days is fine, but include an interim monitoring report at 30 days so we can see if usage is diverging materially.

If Solaris pushes for 15% and unlimited SLA exposure, escalate to me; otherwise present the 12% offer with the true-up & capped SLA. Jordan — can you confirm whether they need prepay to hit a specific run-rate trigger (e.g., spend thresholds tied to product features)? That affects whether we consider a 13% middle ground.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: 2-yr prepay discussion — need for swingline + SLA relief

Team —

Reviewed the economics. We can authorize a one-time concession to 13% discount on list for SOL-2026-482 subject to:

1) A 90-day true-up clause (contractual) with payment or credit to reconcile over/under usage.
2) An SLA credit policy limited to one month-equivalent of the invoiced amount across the 6-month observation window (i.e., aggregate exposure <= 100% of a single monthly invoice). Monthly cap remains 30% of that month's invoice.
3) Draft SOW must include the agreed bucketed usage bands (attached workbook) to be used as the reconciliation reference.
4) Legal to include a clause that allows Redwood to migrate Solaris to usage billing if sustained overconsumption (>150% of bucketed forecast for 2 consecutive quarters).

If Jordan gets pushback from Solaris on the 13% vs their requested 15%, escalate to Lauren for exception. I will prepare the commercial term sheet reflecting the 13%/90-day true-up/SLA cap and circulate to Jordan for review.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
